note: The exclusion register (PLAN.md §3). Every tempting parallel that was considered and rejected, with the reason. A catalogue that only records what it accepted cannot be checked; this file is what makes the accepted set falsifiable. Machine candidates that were never plausible are not all listed individually — see `formulaic` batches, which name the shared string and the verses it drew.

categories.wrong-sense: The string matches but the meaning is opposed or unrelated; the parallel is an artifact of English word order.
categories.formulaic: The shared words are KJV connective or narrative boilerplate ('and it came to pass', 'unto them concerning the') that the Book of Mormon uses continuously and that carry no intertextual signal.
categories.common-vocabulary: The shared words are real content words but too widely distributed in the KJV to point at any one verse.
categories.better-source-identified: A genuine link exists at this verse, but to a different source; the rejected candidate is superseded.
categories.insufficient-verbal: A conceptual resemblance with too little verbal contact to adjudicate as a link at any confidence.

'And/wherefore it came to pass' is the Book of Mormon's single most frequent narrative connective and occurs hundreds of times in the KJV. It should never be treated as evidence of dependence on any particular verse, and candidates resting on it alone are excluded throughout this catalogue without further comment.
A standard KJV formula for prayer with no distinctive content. The real link at this verse is to the Exodus pillar-of-fire theophany; see the accepted link.
Ordinary narrative motion. Absalom's return to his own house has no thematic contact with Lehi's.

'Filled with' takes wisdom, the Spirit, fury, and much else across the KJV. Hiram of Tyre being filled with craftsman's wisdom is not a source for Lehi being filled with the Spirit.

This is the most instructive rejection in the chapter. Proverbs 12:10 gave the longest contiguous match in the machine's candidate set for this verse — five words, scoring 2.00 — and it is wrong. The Proverbs verse reads 'the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel': the phrase is there to be negated, and its subject is the opposite of Nephi's. The true source, Psalm 145:9 ('his tender mercies are over all his works'), shares fewer contiguous words and so never surfaced in the n-gram stream at all, but supplies both halves of Nephi's sentence — the subject 'tender mercies' and the predicate 'over all', a pairing found in no other KJV verse. A longer string match is not a better one, and the contiguous-window method is structurally blind to sources whose agreement is split across a clause.

A four-word run of announcement formula. Worth noting for a different reason, however: the 1830 text spells it 'shew', exactly as the KJV does, and the 1920 edition modernized it to 'show'. The orthography is evidence about the Book of Mormon's relation to KJV English generally, and belongs in the variant register rather than here as a link to any particular verse.
